metadata.source: U.S. Census Bureau ACS 5-Year Data Profiles & Morris County 2026 Certified Rolls

zipCodeComparison.neighborhoodsIncluded: Main St Historic Core & Bartholdi Section, Kiel Avenue & High Street Ridge
keyFindings: Certified composite property tax rate is 3.42%, with an equalization ratio of 71.2%.
Public education represents 63.4% of property taxes, while municipal operations account for 26.6%.
Average residential assessment is $309,720, producing an average annual tax bill of $10,592.42.

neighborhoods.name: Main St Historic Core & Bartholdi Section
neighborhoods.character: Historic industrial rubber manufacturing borough (Pequannock Rubber Co) with classic single-family homes, ranches, and town electric utility
neighborhoods.description: Historic Morris County borough operating its own municipal electric utility (Butler Electric), serving multiple surrounding Highlands towns.
neighborhoods.taxDynamic: Municipal electric utility surplus offsets local municipal government tax levies.

neighborhoods.name: Kiel Avenue & High Street Ridge
neighborhoods.character: Elevated residential streets with single-family ranches, colonials, and wooded yards overlooking Pequannock valley
neighborhoods.description: Quiet hilltop residential section offering wooded views and convenient access to local parks.
neighborhoods.taxDynamic: Steady residential assessments with low municipal tax burden.

equityAnalysis.summary: Butler Borough maintains a certified residential tax roll across its neighborhoods.

keyTakeaways.title: Property Tax Burden & Household Income
keyTakeaways.detail: In Butler Borough, homeowners pay an average of $10,592.42 annually in property taxes, consuming approximately 10.99% of median household income.

keyTakeaways.title: Equalization Ratio & Revaluation Balance
keyTakeaways.detail: With an equalization ratio of 71.2%, assessed values average ~71.2% of current true market values, establishing the basis for certified county tax equalization.

keyTakeaways.title: School District vs Municipal Levy Split
keyTakeaways.detail: Local education represents 63.4% of the total tax bill, municipal government absorbs 26.6%, and Morris County claims 10.0%.
